title: Real Uses of Electronics Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav waits at a foggy airport where nobody can see the runway, yet the planes keep landing safely. How does the control tower see them? In this animated lesson we show that every application of electronics is the same chain of blocks: sense, process, act. Then we follow one real chain in each field: a phone call (microphone, amplifier, transmitter, antenna, and back to a speaker), a television, radar in defence, automatic temperature control in industry, and the ECG machine in medicine.

On a live breadboard the radar sends a pulse, the echo comes back, and the oscilloscope shows the gap between them. We derive d = ct/2 step by step and work out that an echo after 400 microseconds means the plane is 60 km away. A control loop keeps a factory oven at its set temperature while the graph draws live, and an ECG amplifier turns a heart signal of about one millivolt into a trace you can see. Then the exam trap (forgetting to divide by two), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 4 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 1: Introduction to Electronics (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
